record_type_quote: The aim of the study was to investigate the reproducibility of the injury risk model proposed in our previous research (Chalmers et al. 2017; derivation study) that showed an increased injury risk for elite junior Australian football players demonstrating ≥2 asymmetrical FMS subtests. We used a direct replication design.

targets.authors: Chalmers S, Fuller JT, Debenedictis TA, et al.
targets.title: Asymmetry during preseason functional movement screen testing is associated with injury during a junior Australian football season
targets.evidence_quote: The aim of the study was to investigate the reproducibility of the injury risk model proposed in our previous research (Chalmers et al. 2017; derivation study) that showed an increased injury risk for elite junior Australian football players demonstrating ≥2 asymmetrical FMS subtests. targets.outcome_quote: Subjectively, researchers were in agreement that the findings from the derivation data were not successfully reproduced.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly judge their independent replication unsuccessful.
